config.grain_rationale: One row is one entity's tax information for one income year (Name + ABN). The identifiers and name describe the business participant; the monetary amounts and income year are financial facts about that entity-year and have no ontology target.

record_id.rationale: No column combination is a reliable unique key: ABN+Income year collided on the held-out partition (8 duplicate keys) because an ABN can be reported more than once for the same income year. Content hash over all six reported columns is used instead.

fields.rationale: Header is 'Name' in an ATO register of entities reporting tax; values are registered-style legal names ending in PTY LTD / PTY LIMITED / LIMITED. ATO publishes the registered entity name, not a trading name, so legal_name is appropriate.
Column 'ABN' holds 11-digit values with a 100% checksum-valid rate on the discovery partition; validated with the abn transform.

constants.rationale: Australian Taxation Office register of Australian entities identified by ABN; all records are Australian.

unmapped.reason: Monetary amount reported for the income year; no ontology target for financial figures.

config.notes: Workbook has three sheets: 'Information' (documentation), 'Income tax details' (mapped here) and 'PRRT details' (Name, ABN, PRRT Payable) - the PRRT sheet was not mapped; it is a separate small table of petroleum resource rent tax payers. No dates in the data, so the record envelope uses resource_last_modified. ABN+Income year is not unique (an ABN can be reported more than once per income year; the held-out partition had 8 such collisions), so record identity uses content_hash over all six columns. ABN is missing in ~0.9% of rows, so such rows hash with an empty ABN and still emit legal_name.
